name: 29103-batchdecode-dsv4flashfp8-tp8
model: sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 -- the repackaged FP8 build, which is the one that supports data-parallel attention on Hopper (the stock FP4 Hopper path is tensor-parallel only).
parallelism: TP=8 with DP=8 data-parallel attention on one node -- one attention replica per card, each owning its own requests -- over a MoE whose 256 experts are tensor-sharded across the same eight cards. EP=1, a2a backend `none`, PP=1, no router, no external cache tier.
architecture: DeepseekV4ForCausalLM: 43 decoder layers, hidden 4096, MLA-compressed KV (512 + 64 per token per layer, fp8, ~24.8 KiB per token), DeepSeek sparse attention, 256 routed experts at top-6 plus 1 shared, block-FP8 weights, ~294 GB of safetensors so ~36.8 GB per card at TP8.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=512, warmup the first 25%, bounded at 4096 requests with a 2400 s safety cap; 512 streams is 64 concurrent requests per attention replica and `max-running-requests` in sglang-config.yaml must move with it or the engine, not the client, decides the batch.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, SINGLE TURN, no prefix buckets and no prefix reuse: 1024 prompt tokens in and 1024 generated out, both FIXED (stdev 0), with `ignore_eos: true`, `max_tokens: 1024` and `temperature: 0.0`, so every request produces all 1024 tokens.
purpose: A long-form content generator writing 1024-token answers for 512 concurrent users on one eight-GPU node.
launch:
# The engine's command line: sglang at the pinned commit, eight H100s of one node.

# ~294 GB of safetensors, not in the local HF cache -- it downloads once before the run.
model-path: sgl-project/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8

# The checkpoint ships its own config/tokenizer classes.
trust-remote-code: true

# Data-parallel attention over a tensor-parallel MoE. `moe-a2a-backend` and `ep-size` are
# DELIBERATELY ABSENT, so the MoE stays tensor-parallel with no expert parallelism.
tp-size: 8
dp-size: 8
enable-dp-attention: true

kv-cache-dtype: fp8_e4m3

# `chunked-prefill-size` and `max-running-requests` are GLOBAL budgets that the engine divides by
# dp-size, so these are 8192 tokens and 64 requests per card. `max-running-requests` cannot be
# left unset: the DeepSeek-V4 arg hook pins it to 256 when it is None, which would cap the node at
# half the declared concurrency with the rest of the streams queued.
chunked-prefill-size: 65536
disable-radix-cache: true
max-running-requests: 512

# 0.85 rather than the default: an 80 GB card must leave room for CUDA graphs and for the
# per-step buffers a 65536-token global chunk implies.
mem-fraction-static: 0.85
